The following is an overview of these site-specific hypertrophy assessments: circumference measurements, ultrasound, CT, MRI, and biopsy. As in the section on indirect hypertrophy measures, these sections discuss the basic procedures, advantages, and disadvantages associated with each method and the research on the validity of drawing morphological inferences about muscle mass.

## Circumference Measurements

Circumference (girth) measurements are by far the crudest site-specific assessment for hypertrophy. The technique involves placing a flexible tape measure, generally made of cloth, over an area of the body and measuring its girth (). Measurements are commonly taken at the midpoint of the body area, but any site along the muscle can be assessed.
